 Tip came in days before Danielle Lopez's remains were found in NJ forest 
 New details emerge after Danielle Lopez's remains were found in the NJ Pine Barrens, more than two years after she was reported missing. 
 By Isabel Sánchez , Emily Rose Grassi and Siobhan McGirl • 
 Published November 16, 2026 • 
 Updated 4 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Danielle Lopez’s body was found in the Pine Barrens more than two years after her car got stuck in a remote area of New Jersey’s Pine Barrens. NBC10’s Isabel Sanchez has the story. 
 The remains of Danielle Lopez, a 37-year-old woman who disappeared in the New Jersey Pine Barrens more than two years ago, were discovered Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Brendan Byrne State Forest. 
 Lopez disappeared in April 2024 after her vehicle became stuck in a remote area of the Pine Barrens. Her mother, Sue Quackenbush, spent more than two years searching for answers.

 James Ramsey, a private investigator with NJPI Agency who joined the search about a year and a half ago, said his team had started its investigation from scratch, interviewing witnesses and revisiting the area where Lopez was last seen.
 "So information came in late last week to my agency that was shared with the state police of a possible location of Danielle," Ramsey said.
 According to Ramsey, state police already had a large-scale search planned when the information came in. 
 Lopez's remains were discovered Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Brendan Byrne State Forest, an area investigators had previously searched.

 Ramsey said the dense, rugged terrain of the Pine Barrens made the search particularly challenging.
 "Anyone who knows what the Pine Barrens in Jersey, it's a labyrinth," Ramsey said. "It's a needle in a haystack."
 Throughout the search, Quackenbush remained determined to find her daughter.
 "She has been advocating for Danielle all day, every day, since the day she reported her missing. And she doesn't stop, she's relentless," Ramsey said.
 While the discovery brings an end to more than two years of searching, questions remain about how Lopez died. The investigation into her death is ongoing.
 Erica Morse, who works with the Doe Network, an organization that helps bring attention to missing person cases, said finding a missing loved one doesn't necessarily bring closure to a grieving family.
 "There's no such thing as closure in a situation like this, especially for a mom who's already lost two other children," Morse said.
 Morse said families often spend years searching for answers, sometimes making that search their life's mission. She hopes the attention surrounding Lopez's case will also help other families still looking for missing loved ones.
 "But the more people who speak up, the more people who cover this, the more chances we have to bring every one of them home and either reunite them with their loved ones or give them a final resting place," Morse said.
 NBC10 reached out to Quackenbush, who said she is grieving and asked for time.
 The cause of Lopez's death remains unknown as the investigation continues.
 If you have any information about Danielle's case, please contact the New Jersey State Police Missing Persons Unit at 609-882-2000, extension 2554.
 Her story was featured on  Dateline’s newest season of their podcast series, “Missing in America.” 
 This story was originally reported for broadcast by NBC Philadelphia. AI tools helped convert the story to a digital article, and an NBC Philadelphia journalist edited the article for publication.
